doc.title: Dave Bailey and John McNeil Interview, 1959-10-25

title: Trombonist Bill Matthews and growing old
summary: McNeil names Bill Matthews as an active trombonist; talk drifts to age and Bailey never complaining of being tired.

story.theme_name: Illness, injury and the deaths of colleagues
story.community_name: Illness, injury and death among jazz musicians

blocks.x: Do you remember any trombone players from back in those times? No. I don't know. You remember any trombone players from back in those times?
You remember any trombone players from back in those times?
That kid the whole trombone player.

The only one I know that's still active is, that I know of is Bill Matthews. Oh yeah. He used to play the silver standard. I was listening to him when he practiced, wake out a little bit yesterday. I was around in his neighborhood. Where he live in? Mylon Street.

That's where Bill Matthews lived in. He used to live right down in the area. He moved up though. He bought his home and everything. Yeah, his nice place, that beautiful home. I haven't been up there yet.
You got a wife? Yeah, uh-huh.
Yeah. I collect next door from them.
You got children? No, I don't have any children. Just him and his wife.

Yeah. I think he looks well to him. He ought to have a good age on him too. Yeah, yeah, yeah. He ought to be more than 40 years old. Oh, he's way up. He's way up in his late 50s. Because you know the longer we lived in this world, the only way bound to give.
I tell him I don't care if I lived so long to look like a monkey. No difference. The role is honor. You can't stay young man.
No, that's right. You know, I'm a kid. You know, I'm a kid.

You know, I'm a kid. You know, I'm a kid. You know, I'm a kid. You know, I'm a kid. You know, I'm a kid. You know, I'm a kid. You know, I'm a kid. But dear talk about them tired. Then people told me, ladies told me the other day, they said, my God, did you ever stop the other day? I said, sure. I said, I killed them for the time working me. They always complaining, the young fellas, I'm tired. Never hear me talk about them tired.
